A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Matching content across the bibliography-driven pagination shift supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A/C report original quadratic-loss simulations, two-layer ReLU experiments, and CIFAR-10/ResNet-18 results, including Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulations and neural-network experiments, including the CIFAR-10/ResNet-18 results in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The SGD, random-perturbation, and SAM update rules, fixed-alpha approximation, and two-layer ReLU construction are unchanged. No algorithmic component or procedure is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic quadratic losses, the binary-input two-layer ReLU task, and CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18. The larger-model experiments in Appendix A were already present in v1.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the same SGD, random-perturbation, and SAM comparisons. Tables 1–2 retain the same SGD and SAM-radius variants; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The experimental settings remain identical, including the 1,000-step divergence test in C.3, model sizes and hyperparameters in C.4–C.5, and the 200-epoch CIFAR-10 experiment and PCA protocol in Appendix A.

E4.justification: The sensitivity analyses of SAM radius, solution complexity, learning rate, and contrast-loss strength are retained in Figures 1 and 4. The coherence trajectories and supplementary analyses in Appendix C.2 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: C.3 still specifies 10 trials per configuration, and C.4 retains same-seed comparisons averaged over five runs. Table 2 preserves the same plus/minus reporting, without additional uncertainty procedures or run information.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–4 contain the same results and curves. For example, Table 2 retains feature ranks of 148.33 ± 3.22 for SGD and 128.67 ± 5.51 for SAM with radius 0.2.

T1.justification: The definitions, Theorems 3.1–3.6, and appendix derivations and proofs are mathematically unchanged. Updating the Bhatia citation year in Lemma C.6 does not alter its statement or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about coherence governing stability, the emergence of simplicity bias, and SAM strengthening that bias. Contribution scope and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of SAM, coherence, and random-perturbation behavior are retained. Appendix A preserves the same limitations concerning local approximations, data redundancy, optimizer scope, and scalable coherence computation.

D1.justification: Checklist item 5 changes from 'No' and a promise of future code release to 'Yes' with a repository link. Both abstracts already contain that link and claim availability, so this corrects inconsistent access reporting rather than establishing a new release. Implementation details are unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds Mulayoff and Michaeli (2024) as closely related stability work and replaces Chen and Flammarion (2022) with the already-cited Chen et al. (2023). Other reference edits mainly update metadata or consolidate duplicate entries; the broader positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are concentrated in bibliography metadata, citation labels and years, and the code-access checklist response. The main narrative, section organization, and appendix explanations are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Expanded venue and URL entries reflow the bibliography from two pages to three, with local wrapping changes in the checklist and related work. Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–2 retain their displays and captions.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the contradiction between the abstract and checklist about code availability, consolidates duplicate references, and acknowledges additional closely related stability research. These provide modest gains in consistency and bibliographic completeness. The methods, proofs, and empirical evidence remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish a new code release.
